en: A plant of certain species of the genus Brassica, or of related genera (especially Sinapis alba, in the family Brassicaceae, with yellow …

mustard.ety: From Middle English mustard, from Old French moustarde (French moutarde), from moust (“must”), from Latin mustum. Compare Saterland Frisian Muster (“mustard”), Dutch mosterd (“mustard”), German Low German Musterd (“mustard”), Icelandic mustarður (“mustard”). Displaced Middle English senep, from Old English senep, from Latin sināpi (“mustard”). Sometimes mistakenly thought to come from Latin mustum ardens, but such a Latin phrase is not attested, and it is well understood that that the final -ard is derived from Old French -arde. Doublet of mostarda.

ex.en: These facts are mutually related.
ex.ja: この事実はお互いに関連し合っている。

ex.en: The two qualities are mutually exclusive.
ex.ja: その２つの性質は相容れない。

note.ja: mutual（相互の）+ -ly。ラテン語 mutuus（交換された）、mutare（変える）。「互いに」。

en: To plan, control and record the position and course of a vehicle, ship, aircraft, etc., on a journey; to follow a planned course.
To give directions, as from a map, to someone driving a vehicle.

navigate.ety: First attested in 1588; borrowed from Latin nāvigātus, the perfect passive participle of nāvigō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from nāvis (“ship”) + -igō, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂us (“boat”).

note.ja: ラテン語 navigare ＝ navis（船）+ agere（動かす）。「船を操る」→「道をたどる・切り抜ける」。navy と同じ。

en: Extremely overweight, especially: weighing more than 20% (for men) or 25% (for women) over their conventionally ideal weight determined b…
A person who is obese.

obese.ety: From Latin obēsus, derived from obedō (“to devour, eat away”), from ob (“away”) + edō (“to eat”).

note.ja: ラテン語 obesus（食べて太った）から。ob + edere（食べる）。obesity と同じ。

en: The act of reaching out.
The act of raising awareness.
To reach further than.
To surpass or exceed.

outreach.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *úd
Proto-Germanic *ūt
Proto-Germanic *ūt-
Old English ūt-
Middle English ut-
English out-
English reach
English outreach
From out- + reach.

note.ja: out（外へ）+ reach（手を伸ばす）。「外へ手を差し伸べること」→「支援活動・出張サービス」。

en: A vista or point that gives a view down toward something else.
To offer a view (of something) from a higher position.
To fail to notice; to look over and beyond (anything) without seeing it.

overlook.ety:
Inherited from Middle English overloken.
From Middle English overloken; equivalent to over- + look.

ex.en: This kind of mistake is easy to overlook.
ex.ja: この種の間違いは見逃しやすい。

ex.en: These kinds of mistakes are easy to overlook.
ex.ja: この種の間違いは見逃しやすい。

ex.en: I liked the room overlooking the valley.
ex.ja: 私は谷間を見下ろす部屋が好きだった。

note.ja: over（上から・越えて）+ look。「見下ろす」と「見落とす・大目に見る」の両方の意味がある。

en: Of a disease: epidemic over a wide geographical area and affecting a large proportion of the population; also, of or pertaining to a dise…
A pandemic disease; a disease that affects a wide geographical area and a large proportion of the population.
The COVID-19 pandemic.

pandemic.ety: From Ancient Greek πάνδημος (pándēmos, “of or belonging to all the people, public”) + English -ic (suffix forming adjectives from nouns with the sense ‘of or pertaining to’). πάνδημος is derived from παν- (pan-, prefix meaning ‘all, every’) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”)) + δῆμος (dêmos, “the common people; free citizens, sovereign people”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂- (“to divide, share”)). Compare Late Latin pandēmus (“affecting all the people, general, public”).

ex.en: What is a pandemic?
ex.ja: パンデミックって何？

ex.en: What's the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
ex.ja: エピデミックとパンデミックって、何が違うの？

note.ja: pan（すべての）+ dem（民衆）+ ic。すべての人々に広がる →「世界的大流行（の）」。epidemic（民衆の間の流行）より範囲が広い。

en: The sum of the distance of all the lengths of the sides of an object.
The length of such a boundary.

perimeter.ety: From Latin perimetros, Ancient Greek περίμετρος (perímetros). Equivalent to peri- + meter.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 perimetros ＝ peri（周り）+ metron（尺度）。「周りの長さ」→「周囲・外周」。

en: A very long spear used two-handed by infantry soldiers for thrusting (not throwing), both for attacks on enemy foot soldiers and as a cou…
A sharp, pointed staff or implement.
To prod, attack, or injure someone with a pike.
To assume a pike position.

pike.ety:
From Middle English pyke, pyk, pik, pike (“pike; sharp point, iron tip of a staff or spear, pointed toe of an item of footwear; sharp tool; mountain, peak”), from Old English pīc (“pointed object, pick axe”), and Middle French pique (“long thrusting weapon”), from Old French pic (“sharp point, spike”); both ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *pīk, from Proto-Germanic *pīkaz, *pīkō (“sharp point, pike, peak”), related to pick with a narrower meaning.
The word is cognate with Middle Dutch pecke, peke, picke (modern Dutch piek), German Pike, Norwegian pik, Danish pig, and possibly Old Irish pīk.

note.ja: 古英語 pīc（とがったもの）から。「槍」→ 口のとがった魚 →「カワカマス」。peak、pick と同系。

en: Someone who preaches a worldview, philosophy, or religion, especially someone who preaches the gospel and especially a clergyman or clerg…

preacher.ety:
From Middle English precher, prechere; partly equivalent to preach + -er, and partly continuing Middle English prechour, prechiour, from Old French preecheor (French prêcheur), from Latin praedicator (“public praiser, proclaimer”). See preach.
Displaced native Old English bydel.

ex.en: Bob became a preacher.
ex.ja: ボブは牧師になりました。

note.ja: preach + -er。「説教者」。

en: To go before, go in front of.
To cause to be preceded; to preface; to introduce.
Brief editorial preface (usually to an article or essay).

precede.ety: From Middle French précéder, from Latin praecēdō, from prae- + cēdō.

ex.en: A rich life is always preceded by disaster.
ex.ja: 壊滅そのものが豊かな生命を生む。

ex.en: The rain was preceded by wind.
ex.ja: 雨になる前に風が吹いた。

ex.en: Your reputation precedes you.
ex.ja: お噂はかねがね伺っております。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ ced（行く）+ e。前に行く →「先立つ・先行する」。precedent（前例）。

en: The purchasing department of a company.
The act of procuring or obtaining; obtainment; attainment.

procurement.ety: Inherited from Middle English procurement, from Old French procurement, from procurer.

ex.en: We are trying to clarify your future procurement requirements.
ex.ja: お客様の今後の購買需要を明らかにしようとしています。

note.ja: procure（調達する）+ -ment。pro（代わりに）+ curare（世話をする）。「世話をして手に入れること」→「調達」。cure と同じ cur。

en: Someone who protects or guards, by assignment or on their own initiative.
A headmate who primarily fronts, or otherwise protects the system, in situations where the system is at risk of psychological harm.

protector.ety: From Middle English protectour, from Anglo-Norman protectour, protector and its etymon Latin prōtēctor, from prōtegō (“shield, protect”). By surface analysis, protect + -or. Displaced native Old English sċildend.

ex.en: Is there a protector on the part that is spinning?
ex.ja: 回っている部分にプロテクターはあるか？

note.ja: protect + -or。「保護者・プロテクター」。

en: A mixture of wood, cellulose and/or rags and water ground up to make paper.
A mass of chemically processed wood fibres (cellulose).
To make or be made into pulp.
To deprive of pulp; to separate the pulp from.
Of or pertaining to pulp magazines; in the style of a pulp magazine or the material printed within such a publication.

pulp.ety: From Middle English pulpe, from Latin pulpa.

ex.en: They beat the dog to a pulp.
ex.ja: 彼らはその犬をめったうちにした。

ex.en: Reduce to pulp by boiling.
ex.ja: くたくたに煮る。

note.ja: ラテン語 pulpa（果肉）から。「果肉・パルプ」→ 安いパルプ紙の雑誌 →「低俗小説」。

en: Money paid for the freeing of a hostage.
The release of a captive, or of captured property, by payment of a consideration.
To pay a price to set someone free from captivity or punishment.
To exact a ransom (payment) in exchange for the freedom of.

From the Middle English raunsoun, from the Old French raençon, from stem of Latin redēmptiō. Entered English ca. the 13th century. Doublet of redemption.

ex.en: The hijacker demanded a ransom of two million dollars.
ex.ja: 乗っ取り犯人は２００万ドルの身の代金を要求した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rançon（買い戻し）から。ラテン語 redemptio。redemption と同じ語源。「身代金」。

en: A shaky or unsteady gait.
A lively dance originating in Scotland.
To wind on a reel.
To spin or revolve repeatedly.

reel.ety: From Middle English reel, reele, from Old English rēol, hrēol, from Proto-West Germanic *hrehul, from Proto-Germanic *hrehulaz, *hrahilaz, from Proto-Indo-European *krek- (“to weave, beat”). Cognate with Icelandic ræl, hræll.

ex.en: He reeled in a huge fish yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日彼は大きな魚を釣り上げました。

ex.en: My punch sent him reeling.
ex.ja: 私のパンチで彼はよろめいた。

ex.en: My punch sent him reeling into the rope.
ex.ja: 私のパンチは彼をロープに追い込んだ。

note.ja: 古英語 hrēol（糸巻き）から。「リール」→ 糸巻きのようにくるくる回る →「よろめく」。

en: The practising of something which is to be performed before an audience, usually to test or improve the interaction between several parti…
A preparatory activity analogous to a rehearsal (sense 1).

rehearsal.ety: From Middle English rehercel, rehersail, rehersall, from rehersen and apparently partly Middle French rehercel. By surface analysis, rehearse + -al.

ex.en: With the extra rehearsals, work is really tight.
ex.ja: リハの回数増えたから仕事キチキチだよ。

ex.en: Just right now, I'm doing a rehearsal for the concert.
ex.ja: ちょうど今、コンサートのリハーサルをしています。

ex.en: After a ten-minute break, we resumed our rehearsal.
ex.ja: １０分休憩してからまたリハーサルを続けました。

note.ja: rehearse（下稽古する）+ -al。古フランス語 rehercier（再び耕す）、herse（まぐわ）。「何度も繰り返すこと」→「リハーサル」。hearse（霊柩車）も同じ herse。

en: To strengthen, especially by addition or augmentation.
To emphasize or review.

reinforce.ety:
Etymology tree

Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English inforce
English reinforce
From re- + inforce.

note.ja: re（再び）+ inforce（強くする）。force（力）。「再び力を加える」→「強化する」。

en: The act of starting something again.
To start again.
Synonym of reboot.

English restart
From re- + start.

ex.en: You need to restart your PC.
ex.ja: PCを再起動する必要があります。

ex.en: You need to restart your computer.
ex.ja: PCを再起動する必要があります。

ex.en: Please restart your computer.
ex.ja: コンピューターを再起動してください。

note.ja: re（再び）+ start（始める）。「再開する・再起動する」。

en: To cause (a person or animal) to recover from a faint; to cause (a person or animal) to return to a state of consciousness.
To bring (a person or animal which is dead) back to life.

revive.ety: The verb is derived from Late Middle English reviven, revyven (“to recover from illness; to regain consciousness; to return to life after death; to happen again, recur; to be rejuvenated, renewed; (figurative) to bring back; (alchemy) of a metal: to be restored to its original form”), from Anglo-Norman reviver, revivre (“to return to life after death; to rejuvenate, renew; to make (a law or legal document) valid again”), Middle French revivre, and Old French revivre (“to return to life after death; to rejuvenate, renew”) (modern French revivre), and directly from their etymon Latin revīvere, t

ex.en: That rose will revive if you water it.
ex.ja: 水をやればそのバラは生き返るでしょう。

ex.en: The plants will revive after a good rain.
ex.ja: 慈雨があれば草木は生き返るでしょう。

ex.en: I was revived by a glass of water.
ex.ja: 私は一杯の水で生き返った。

note.ja: re（再び）+ viv（生きる）+ e。再び生きる →「生き返らせる・復活させる」。

en: Showing, causing, or favoring rigour/rigor; scrupulously accurate or strict; thorough.
Severe; intense.

rigorous.ety: Inherited from Middle English rigorous, from Middle French and Anglo-Norman rigoreus, derived from Late Latin rigōrōsus (stiff, rigid; inflexible). By surface analysis, rigor + -ous.

ex.en: The top engineer put the car through a series of rigorous tests.
ex.ja: トップエンジニアが、その車に一連の厳重な検査を加えた。

note.ja: ラテン語 rigor（硬さ）から。硬く厳しい →「厳格な・厳密な」。

en: A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.
A headscarf.
To throw on loosely; to put on like a scarf.
To dress with a scarf, or as with a scarf; to cover with a loose wrapping.

scarf.ety: Probably from Old Northern French escarpe (compare Old French escharpe (“pilgrim's purse suspended from the neck”), which see). The verb is derived from the noun. Doublet of scrip.

ex.en: The girl has a scarf around her neck.
ex.ja: その女の子は首のまわりにスカーフを巻いている。

ex.en: She has a scarf around her neck.
ex.ja: 彼女は首にスカーフをまいている。

ex.en: Put your scarf on. It's cold out.
ex.ja: マフラーをしなさい。外は寒いわ。

note.ja: 古北フランス語 escarpe（肩掛けかばん）から。「スカーフ」。

en: View, natural features, landscape.
Stage backdrops, property and other items on a stage that give the impression of the location of the scene.

scenery.ety: Earlier scenary, from scene + -ary, but now remodelled as scene + -ery.

ex.en: The beauty of the scenery is beyond description.
ex.ja: その景色の美しさは筆舌に尽くしがたい。

ex.en: He was excited to see the beautiful scenery.
ex.ja: 彼はその美しい光景を見てわくわくした。

ex.en: This district is known for its beautiful scenery.
ex.ja: この地方は美しい風景で知られている。

note.ja: scene（場面）+ -ery。ギリシャ語 skēnē（テント・舞台）。「舞台の背景」→「景色」。

Conveying nerve impulses from the sense organs to the nerve centers.

ex.ja: 正常な感覚的知識を定義するのは困難であるし、おそらく、不可能でさえあるだろう。

note.ja: sense（感覚）+ -ory。「感覚の」。

en: A paved footpath located at the side of a road, for the use of pedestrians.
Any paved footpath, even if not located at the side of a road.

ex.ja: 歩道は落ち葉で覆われていた。

ex.en: You shouldn't ride a bicycle on the sidewalk.
ex.ja: 歩道で自転車に乗ってはいけません。

note.ja: side（わき）+ walk（歩く所）。「道のわきの歩く所」→「歩道」。

Of or relating to philosophical skepticism or the skeptics.

ex.ja: 私は、5つ以上の言語を流暢に話せるという主張には、疑いを持ちます。

note.ja: skeptic（懐疑論者）+ -al。ギリシャ語 skeptikos（考え深い）、skeptesthai（よく見る）。「疑い深い」。scope と同系。

en: Tired; feeling the need for sleep.
Suggesting tiredness.
The gum that builds up in the eye; sleep, gound.
Shingleback.
To sleep.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian släipich (“sleepy”), West Frisian sliepich (“sleepy”), dialectal Dutch slapig, slepig (“sleepy”), German Low German slapig, släpig, slöpig (“sleepy”), archaic German schlafig (“sleepy”).

ex.en: I'm sleepy. Can you read me a story?
ex.ja: 眠い。本読んで。

ex.en: I'm so sleepy I'm about to fall over.
ex.ja: 眠すぎて倒れそう。

ex.en: I'm sleepy. I'm going to sleep. Good night.
ex.ja: 眠くなった。寝る。ぐない。

note.ja: sleep + -y。「眠い」→ 町が「活気のない」。

en: In a smooth manner; smooth.

smoothly.ety: From Middle English smoþely; equivalent to smooth + -ly.

ex.en: Their married life did not run smoothly.
ex.ja: 彼らの結婚生活はうまくいかなかった。

ex.en: Well it will probably go smoothly.
ex.ja: 多分うまく行くさ。

ex.en: I think communication is what makes an organization run smoothly.
ex.ja: コミュニケーションは組織の潤滑油だと思います。

note.ja: smooth + -ly。「滑らかに・順調に」。

en: A town containing merchants who have exclusive right, under royal authority, to purchase or produce certain goods for export; also, the b…
Place of supply; source.
To sort according to its staple.
Relating to, or being market of staple for, commodities.
Established in commerce; occupying the markets; settled.

ex.en: Coffee is one of the staples of Brazil.
ex.ja: コーヒーはブラジルの主要産物の一つである。

ex.ja: ホチキスの針って、どうやって入れればいいの？

ex.ja: ホチキスの針って、どうやって入れればいいの？

en: A conventional, formulaic, and often oversimplified or exaggerated conception, opinion, or image of (a person or a group of people).
A person who is regarded as embodying or conforming to a set image or type.
To make a stereotype of someone or something, or characterize someone by a stereotype.
To prepare for printing in stereotype; to produce stereotype plates of.
Of an edition: printed in stereotype.

ex.ja: この番組はマンネリになっている。

ex.en: The movie is a stereotyped sob story.
ex.ja: その映画はお涙頂戴ものだ。

en: Unable to act or respond; dazed; shocked.

ex.en: The people around were stunned.
ex.ja: 周りの人は呆然としていた。

ex.ja: 彼の辞任を知って、彼らは呆然とした。

ex.en: Grandmother died, leaving the whole family stunned.
ex.ja: おばあちゃんが突然死んで家族一同驚いた。

note.ja: stun（気絶させる）+ -ed。「呆然とした」。stunning と同じ。

en: A Japanese dish made of small portions of sticky white rice flavored with vinegar, usually wrapped in seaweed and filled or topped with f…
Raw fish, especially as a Japanese dish.
To prepare (a food) as sushi.

Desire for revenge.

ex.en: I am Finnish, but I speak also Swedish.
ex.ja: 私はフィンランド人なのに、スウェーデン語も話せる。

note.ja: Finn + -ish。「フィンランドの・フィンランド語」。

en: Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus (definite location).
Belonging to, concerning, or located at a focus of attention.
An object that is used to focus concentration when performing magic.
The individual who is the focus of a study or review, when the study or review is based on that individual's interactions with others.

focal.ety: Learned borrowing from New Latin focālis. By surface analysis, focus + -al.

note.ja: focus（焦点）+ -al。「焦点の・中心の」。

en: A permanent military post.
The troops stationed at such a post.
To assign troops to a military post.
To convert into a military fort.

garrison.ety: From Middle English garisoun, garysoun, from Old French garison, guarison, from guarir + -ison, ultimately of Germanic origin; thus a doublet of warison. Compare guard, ward; the modern meaning is influenced by (now obsolete) garnison.

ex.en: The garrison was forced to surrender.
ex.ja: 守備隊は降伏を強いられた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 garison（守ること）から。garir（守る）。「守備隊・駐屯地」。guard と同系。

en: In a glad manner; happily.
Willingly; certainly.

gladly.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *gladaz
Proto-West Germanic *glad
Old English glæd
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Old English glædlīċe
Middle English gladly
English gladly
Inherited from Middle English gladly (“joyousuly, voluntarily, easily”), from Old English glædlīċe (“gladly, pleasantly, kindly”), from glæd (“glad, bright”) + -līċe. Compare Danish glædelig (“joyful”), Icelandic gleðilegur (“delightful”). More at glad, -ly.

ex.en: I'd gladly speak with you on this subject.
ex.ja: この件について喜んで相談します。

ex.en: I'd gladly help you, only I'm too busy now.
ex.ja: できれば喜んでお手伝いするのですが、今は忙しすぎるのです。

ex.en: For you, I will do it gladly.
ex.ja: 君のためなら、喜んで。

note.ja: glad + -ly。「喜んで」。

en: A favorably disposed attitude toward someone or something.
The value of a business entity not directly attributable to its tangible assets and liabilities, deriving from factors such as consumer l…
To voluntarily provide or cover some or all of the cost of (something) to maintain goodwill.

goodwill.ety:
From Middle English *goodwille, good wille, possibly from Old English *gōdwille (compare gōdwillende (“well-pleased”)). Compare also Scots guidwilly, guidwillie (“displaying goodwill”). By surface analysis, good + will.
Cognate with Scots guidwill (“goodwill”), Middle Low German gūtwille (“goodwill”), Old High German guotwilligi (“goodwill”), Old Danish godvilje (“goodwill”), Icelandic góðvilji, góðvili (“goodwill”), Icelandic góðvild (“goodness”).
The sense "thrift shop" is a genericized trademark of the US-based chain Goodwill Industries.

ex.en: Your goodwill sank into my heart.
ex.ja: あなたの善意は身にしみました。

note.ja: good（よい）+ will（意志）。「善意」→ 会社の信用 →「のれん」。

en: Proceeding or advancing by small, slow, regular steps or degrees
An antiphon or responsory after the epistle, in the Mass, which was sung on the steps, or while the deacon ascended the steps.
A service book containing the musical portions of the Mass.

gradual.ety: From Medieval Latin graduālis, from Latin gradus (“step”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰradʰ-, *gʰredʰ- (“to walk, go”). Cognate with Gothic 𐌲𐍂𐌹𐌸𐍃 (griþs, “step, grade”), Bavarian Gritt (“step, stride”).

ex.en: Your English has made gradual progress.
ex.ja: 君の英語はだんだんに進歩してきたよ。

ex.en: Computers caused a great, if gradual, change.
ex.ja: コンピューターは、たとえ緩慢にせよ大きな変化を引き起こした。

ex.en: It's a gradual thing.
ex.ja: 少しずつそうなったということですね。

note.ja: ラテン語 gradus（段）から。「一段ずつの」→「徐々の」。gradually と同じ。

en: A restraint or support, especially one consisting of a loop or network of rope or straps, and especially one worn by a working animal suc…
A collection of wires or cables bundled and routed according to their function: a wiring harness.
To place a harness on something; to tie up or restrain.
To capture, control or put to use.

harness.ety: From Middle English harneys, harnes, harneis, harnais, herneis, from Anglo-Norman harneis and Old French hernois (“equipment used in battle”), believed to be from Old Norse *hernest, from herr (“army”) + nest (“provisions”) (from Proto-Germanic *nesaną (“to heal, recover”)). More at harry.

note.ja: 古フランス語 harneis（武具）から。「馬具」→ 馬の力を使う →「（力を）利用する」。

en: One pulsation of the heart; especially an irregular one, hence the emotion which causes it.
The rhythm at which a heart pulsates, a cardiac indicator.

ex.en: The doctor monitored the patient's heartbeat and blood pressure.
ex.ja: 医師は患者の心臓の鼓動と血圧をモニターで監視した。

note.ja: heart（心臓）+ beat（打つこと）。「心拍・鼓動」。

en: UK standard spelling of honorable.
UK standard spelling of honorable.

honourable.ety: From Middle English honourable, from Old French honorable, honurable, from Latin honōrābilis, from honōrō (“to honour”); cognate with Italian onorabile, Spanish honorable. By surface analysis, honour + -able. In this sense, largely displaced Old English ārfæst.

ex.en: I heard a very honourable story from the company president.
ex.ja: 社長からとても光栄なお話を受け賜りました。

ex.en: With that sort of attitude you'll never get past the honourable-mention prizes.
ex.ja: そんなんじゃいつまで経っても奨励賞止まりだぞ？

note.ja: honorable のイギリスのつづり。

en: About to happen, occur, or take place very soon, especially of something which won't last long.

imminent.ety: From the present participle of Latin imminēre (“to overhang”), from mineō ("to project, overhang"), related to minae (English menace) and mons (English mount). Compare with eminent.

ex.en: According to the radio, a storm is imminent in the North.
ex.ja: ラジオによると、北海で嵐が起こるとのことだ。

ex.en: According to the radio, a storm is imminent in the North Sea.
ex.ja: ラジオによると、北海で嵐が起こるとのことだ。

ex.en: A storm is imminent.
ex.ja: 今にも嵐になりそうだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 imminere（上に張り出す・迫る）から。in + minere（突き出す）。「差し迫った」。prominent と同じ。

en: Of inauguration; as in a speech or lecture by the person being inaugurated.
Marking the beginning of an operation, venture, etc.
An inauguration; a formal beginning.

inaugural.ety: From French inaugural, from inaugurer, from Latin augurare (“to take omens”).

note.ja: inaugurate（就任させる）+ -al。ラテン語 inaugurare（鳥占いで始める）。augur（鳥占い師）。古代ローマでは物事を始める前に鳥占いをした。「就任の・最初の」。

en: The act of insulating; detachment from other objects; isolation.
The state of being insulated; detachment from other objects; isolation.

insulation.ety:
Etymology tree
English insulate
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin -ātiōlbor.
Old French -ationbor.
Middle English -acioun
English -ation
English -ion
English insulation
From insulate + -ion.

ex.en: The noise was deadened by the insulation.
ex.ja: 音は防音装置で十分小さくなった。

ex.en: This packaging material provides heat insulation.
ex.ja: この梱包材が断熱機能を担っている。

ex.en: Hirofumi installed fibreglass insulation in the ceiling.
ex.ja: 博文は天井にグラスファイバーの断熱材を入れた。

note.ja: insulate（隔離する・絶縁する）+ -ion。ラテン語 insula（島）。「島のように隔てること」→「断熱・絶縁」。peninsula と同じ insul。

en: A person who is interned, forcibly or voluntarily.
To imprison somebody, usually without trial.
To confine or hold (foreign military personnel who stray into the state's territory) within prescribed limits during wartime.

intern.ety: From French interner, from interne (“inner, internal”), from Latin internus (“within, internal”), compare Etymology 2.

note.ja: フランス語 interne（内部の）から。ラテン語 internus。「（病院などの）内部で働く人」→「実習生」、内部に閉じ込める →「抑留する」。internal と同じ。

en: Lacking a sense of responsibility; performed or acting as though without responsibility; negligent.
Someone who is not responsible.

irresponsible.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Italic *n̥-
Latin in-
Latin ir-
English ir-
English responsible
English irresponsible
From ir- + responsible.

ex.en: The man charged me with being irresponsible.
ex.ja: その男は私を無責任だと非難した。

ex.en: It was irresponsible of him to break a promise.
ex.ja: 約束を破るとは彼も無責任だ。

ex.en: It is irresponsible of you to break your promise.
ex.ja: 約束を破るなんて無責任だ。

note.ja: ir（否定）+ responsible（責任のある）。「無責任な」。respond と同じ spond。

en: Late.
Last made; hence, made of refuse; inferior.
A gap, a delay; an interval created by something not keeping up; a latency.
Delay; latency.
To fail to keep up (the pace), to fall behind.
To cover (for example, pipes) with felt strips or similar material.

lag.ety: Of unknown origin. Possibly of North Germanic origin.

ex.en: He lags behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: He's lagging behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: I've got a bad case of jet lag.
ex.ja: 時差ボケで辛い。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「遅れる」。jet lag（時差ぼけ）。

en: One who lends, especially money; specifically, a bank or other entity that specializes in granting loans.

lender.ety: From Middle English lendare, leendare, variants of lenner, lenere, equivalent to lend + -er.

ex.en: That man borrows money from many lenders.
ex.ja: あの男の人は多重債務者である。

ex.en: Money lenders are enjoying a profitable period.
ex.ja: 資金の貸し手は高利益の時期を享受している。

note.ja: lend（貸す）+ -er。「貸し手」。loan と同系。

en: The fact or quality of having a position in space.
The features or surroundings of a particular place.

locality.ety: From French localité, from Late Latin localitas, equivalent to local + -ity.

ex.en: The locality does not count for much in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本では土地勘というものは、あまり価値がない。

ex.en: Localities imposed bans on development.
ex.ja: いくつかの地方自治体では開発を禁止した。

note.ja: local + -ity。「地域・場所」。

en: Something that tempts or attracts, especially one with a promise of reward or pleasure.
An artificial bait attached to a fishing line to attract fish.
To attract by temptation, appeal, or guile.
To attract fish with a lure.

lure.ety: From Anglo-Norman lure, from Old French loirre (Modern French leurre), from Frankish *lōþr, from Proto-Germanic *lōþr-, perhaps ultimately related to *laþō (“invitation, calling”), or from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (“to hide”). Compare English allure, also from Old French. Probably related to German Luder (“bait”).

ex.en: The dress lured her into the store.
ex.ja: そのドレスにひかれて彼女はその店の中に入った。

ex.en: He lured her away from her husband.
ex.ja: 彼女を夫の手からおびき出した。

ex.en: He felt the lure of adventure.
ex.ja: 彼は冒険の誘惑を感じた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 loirre（鷹を呼び戻すおとり）から。「誘い込む・疑似餌」。

en: Intending to do harm; characterized by spite and malice.

malicious.ety: From Middle English malicious, from Old French malicios, from Latin malitiōsus, from malitia (“malice”), from malus (“bad”). Displaced native Middle English ivelwilled and ivelwilly (“malicious”), related to Old English yfelwillende (literally “evil-willing”). By surface analysis, malice + -ious.

ex.en: Please tell me how to deal with malicious comments.
ex.ja: 陰湿な嫌がらせを受けた場合の対処法について教えてください。

ex.en: Beware of 'One Ring' malicious nuisance calls!!
ex.ja: 悪質な迷惑電話、ワンギリにご注意！！

note.ja: ラテン語 malitia（悪意）から。malus（悪い）。「悪意のある」。malice、malware と同じ mal。

en: A pad on which a person can recline and sleep, usually having an inner section of coiled springs covered with foam or other cushioning ma…
A form of retaining wall used to support foundations or an embankment
To cover with a thick layer, like a mattress; to blanket.

mattress.ety:
Etymology tree
Arabic طَرَحَ (ṭaraḥa)
Arabic مَطْرَح (maṭraḥ)bor.
Old French matrasbor.
Middle English materas
English mattress
From Middle English materas, from Old French matras, from Arabic مَطْرَح (maṭraḥ, “place where something is thrown”), from طَرَحَ (ṭaraḥa, “to throw”). Compare divan, from Persian via Turkish (both of Middle Eastern origin, due to the local custom of lying on padding on floor being foreign to Europeans).

ex.en: Do you really hide your money under the mattress?
ex.ja: 本当にマットレスの下にお金隠してるの？

ex.en: I need a new mattress.
ex.ja: 新しいマットレスがいるな。

ex.en: I hid it under the mattress.
ex.ja: マットレスの下に隠しました。

note.ja: アラビア語 maṭraḥ（敷物・クッション）から、イタリア語を経た語。

en: A naevus, a pigmented, slightly raised, and sometimes hairy spot on the skin.
To create a network of channels in (waterlogged soil) to improve drainage.

mole.ety:
From Middle English mole, mool, from Old English māl (“a mole, spot, mark, blemish”), from Proto-West Germanic *mail, from Proto-Germanic *mailą (“spot, wrinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *mel-, *melw- (“dark, dirty”), from Proto-Indo-European *mey-, *my- (“to soil, sully”).
Cognate with Scots mail (“spot, stain”), Saterland Frisian Moal (“scar”), German dialectal Meil (“spot, stain, blemish”), Gothic 𐌼𐌰𐌹𐌻 (mail, “spot, blemish”).

ex.en: Mary has a mole under her eye.
ex.ja: メアリーには泣きぼくろがある。

ex.en: That person has a mole at the side of his eye.
ex.ja: あの人は眼の横にほくろがある。

ex.en: I don't think people should make a mountain of a mole hill.
ex.ja: 針ほどのことを棒ほどにいうのはどうかと思います。

note.ja: 「ほくろ」は古英語 māl、「モグラ」は中英語 molle からで別語。モグラのように潜り込む →「スパイ」。

en: A government in which sovereignty is embodied within a single, today usually hereditary head of state (whether as a figurehead or as a po…
The territory ruled over by a monarch; a kingdom.

monarchy.ety: From Old French monarchie, from Late Latin monarchia, from Ancient Greek μοναρχία (monarkhía), from μόνος (mónos, “only”) + ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “power, authority”). By surface analysis, mon- (“one, single”) + -archy (“rule, command”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monos（ひとりの）+ archein（治める）。「ひとりが治めること」→「君主制」。monarch。

en: Of, relating to, or connected with muscles.
Brawny, thewy, having strength.

muscular.ety: Late 17th century; from muscle (Latin mūsculus) + -ar. Compare French musculaire.

ex.en: With his muscular constitution he passes for a judoist.
ex.ja: 骨格たくましい体格なので彼は柔道家でとおっている。

ex.en: My muscular strength has weakened from lack of exercise.
ex.ja: 運動不足で筋肉が弱くなった。

ex.en: The bullet penetrated his muscular chest.
ex.ja: 弾丸は彼の厚い胸板を貫通した。

note.ja: muscle（筋肉）+ -ar。ラテン語 musculus（小さなネズミ）。力こぶの動きがネズミに見えたことから。

en: The state or quality of being neutral; the condition of being unengaged in contests between others; state of taking no part on either side.
The quality or state of being neutral.

neutrality.ety: From Middle French neutralité, from Medieval Latin neutralitas. Morphologically neutral + -ity.

ex.en: The alternative possibilities are neutrality or war.
ex.ja: 可能性は中立か戦争かの二つに一つだ。

note.ja: neutral（中立の）+ -ity。「中立」。

en: Making a noise, especially a loud unpleasant sound
Full of noise.

noisy.ety:
Etymology tree
English noise
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English noisy
From noise + -y.

ex.en: I don't like noisy music, such as rock.
ex.ja: 私はうるさい音楽は好きではない。たとえばロックのような。

ex.en: Let's go outside. It's too noisy in here.
ex.ja: 外に行こう。ここは騒がしすぎるよ。

ex.en: That street was very noisy during the day.
ex.ja: その通りは昼間は大変騒がしかった。

note.ja: noise（騒音）+ -y。「騒がしい」。noise はラテン語 nausea（船酔い）から、騒ぎ・不快 →「騒音」とされる。

en: A rush of sexual excitement; now specifically, the climax or peak of sexual pleasure, which occurs during sexual activity and which in ma…
A creamy white alcoholic cocktail containing amaretto, Irish cream, and coffee liqueur.
To have an orgasm.

From French orgasme or New Latin orgasmus, from Ancient Greek ὀργασμός (orgasmós, “excitement, swelling”), from ὀργάω (orgáō, “to swell with moisture”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 orgasmos（興奮）から。organ（ふくらむ）。

en: Underpants for women and girls.

ex.en: I can’t stand panties.
ex.ja: パンツが大嫌いです。

ex.en: Now that you mention it, she also needs a bra and panties.
ex.ja: 店員さんがそう言うなら、ブラジャーとパンティーも買ってってやろう。

note.ja: pants（ズボン・下着）+ -ie（小さい）。pants は pantaloons の短縮。

en: A package wrapped, as for shipment or transport.
An individual consignment of cargo for shipment, regardless of size and form.
To wrap something up into the form of a package.
To wrap a strip around the end of a rope.

parcel.ety: From Middle English parcel, from Old French parcelle (“a small piece or part, a parcel, a particle”), from Late Latin particella, diminutive of Latin particula (“particle”), diminutive of partem (“part, piece”). Doublet of particle.

ex.en: Please take this parcel to the post office.
ex.ja: この小包を郵便局へ持って行ってください。

ex.en: I want to send this parcel at once.
ex.ja: この小包をすぐ送りたい。

ex.en: I want to send a parcel to Japan.
ex.ja: 日本に小包を送りたいのですが。

note.ja: ラテン語 particula（小さな部分）から。part（部分）の仲間。小分けにしたもの →「小包・区画」。

en: An action which divides a thing into parts, or separates one thing from another.
A part of something that has been divided.
To divide something into parts, sections or shares.
To divide a region or country into two or more territories with separate political status.

partition.ety: Recorded c.1430, "division into shares, distinction," from Middle English particioun, from Old French particion (modern partition), from Latin partitio, partitionem (“division, portion”), from partitus, the past participle of partire (“to split (up), part(ition)”).

ex.en: Can a body, hand, or finger enter the safety partition?
ex.ja: 安全用パーテーションに体・手・指が入れるか？

ex.en: The hall could seat a thousand people before it was partitioned.
ex.ja: ホールは仕切りを設ける前は千人収容できた。

ex.en: The bullet penetrated the partition.
ex.ja: 弾丸は仕切り壁を貫いた。

note.ja: part（分ける）+ ition。分けること →「仕切り・分割（する）」。

en: Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual.
Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.
That which is peculiar; a sole or exclusive property; a prerogative; a characteristic.
an ecclesiastical district, parish, chapel or church outside the jurisdiction of the bishop of the diocese in which it is situated.

peculiar.ety: From Latin pecūliāris (“one's own”), from pecūlium (“private property”), from pecus (“cattle”).

ex.en: Can you name any plants peculiar to Japan?
ex.ja: 日本にしかない植物の名を幾つか挙げられますか。

ex.en: The odd custom is peculiar to the region.
ex.ja: その変わった習慣はその地方特有のものだ。

ex.en: This style of cooking is peculiar to China.
ex.ja: この調理法は中国独特のものだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 peculium（自分の財産）から。pecu（家畜）。「自分だけの」→「独特の・変な」。

en: Of or relating to property or ownership.
Owning something; having ownership.
A proprietor or owner.
A body of proprietors, taken collectively.

proprietary.ety: From French propriétaire, from Latin proprietārius. By surface analysis, propriety + -ary. Compare with the Latin proprietas (“property”) and proprius (“ownership”).

ex.en: I've come here today to talk about the dangers of proprietary software.
ex.ja: 今回はプロプライエタリソフトウェアの危険性について話すべくに参りました。

note.ja: ラテン語 proprietarius（所有者の）から。proprius（自分の）。「所有者の・独占的な」→ 特定企業の「独自規格の」。property と同じ。

en: The prostate gland.
Of or relating to the prostate gland.

prostate.ety:

Borrowed from Middle French prostate, a learned borrowing from Medieval Lat

ex.en: I had an enlarged prostate.
ex.ja: 前立腺肥大になりました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 prostatēs（前に立つもの）から。pro（前に）+ histanai（立つ）。「前立腺」。prostrate（ひれ伏す）と混同しやすい。

en: The main character, or one of the main characters, in any story, such as a literary work or drama.
A leading person in a contest; a principal performer.

protagonist.ety:
Etymology tree

assassin.ety:
From either French assassin or Italian assassino, from Arabic أَسَاسِيِّين (ʔasāsiyyīn, “people who are faithful to the foundation [of the faith]”) and the folkloric etymology Arabic حَشَّاشِين (ḥaššāšīn, “hashish users; low-lives”).
The mathematical sense was introduced by Bourbaki, playing on the notation operatorname Ass(M) and the fact that an associated prime is the annihilator of an element, and so is said to kill that element.

note.ja: アラビア語 ḥashshāshīn（大麻を使う者）から。中世の暗殺教団の呼び名。assassination と同じ。

en: A suddenly reversed or backward motion, such as of a rope or elastic band when it snaps under tension.
A negative reaction, objection or outcry, especially of a violent or abrupt nature.
To perform a backlash, to lash back in reaction to some cause.

ex.en: The bribery scandal created a backlash overseas.
ex.ja: 収賄スキャンダルは海外で激しい反発を生みました。

note.ja: back（後ろへ）+ lash（むち打ち）。機械のがたつき・跳ね返り →「反発・反動」。

en: A shared record of past transactions in a distributed network, typically used for cryptocurrency.

blockchain.ety: From block + chain, from earlier “block chain”. In the 2008 Bitcoin paper block and chain are used separately; the concept is referred to as “chain of hash-based proof-of-work” or “chain of digital signatures”.

note.ja: block（塊）+ chain（鎖）。「データのブロックを鎖のようにつないだもの」。

en: A building where beer is produced.
A company that brews beer.

brewery.ety: From Dutch brouwerij (“brewery”), equivalent to brew + -ery. See also brewhouse.

note.ja: brew（醸造する）+ -ery（場所）。「醸造所」。

en: The bulb-shaped underground portion of a plant such as a tulip, consisting of a shortened stem and many fleshy scale leaves, from which t…
Any solid object rounded at one end and tapering on the other, possibly attached to a larger object at the tapered end.
To take the shape of a bulb; to swell.

bulb.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek βολβός (bolbós)bor.
Latin bulbusder.
English bulb
Inherited from Middle English bulb, bolbe, from Latin bulbus (“bulb, onion”), from Ancient Greek βολβός (bolbós, “plant with round swelling on underground stem”).

ex.en: A small, naked bulb gave the only illumination.
ex.ja: 小さな裸電球が唯一の明りだった。

ex.en: The light bulb has burned out.
ex.ja: 電球が切れた。

ex.en: Thomas Edison invented the light bulb.
ex.ja: トマス・エジソンが電球を発明した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 bolbos（タマネギ・球根）から。「球根」→ 球根の形 →「電球」。

en: A wood-based material resembling heavy paper, used in the manufacture of boxes, cartons and signs.
Something flat or insubstantial.
Made of or resembling cardboard.
Flat or flavorless.

ex.en: I need a couple of empty cardboard boxes.
ex.ja: 段ボールが２・３個いるの。

ex.en: Prepare five postcard sized pieces of cardboard.
ex.ja: はがき大のボール紙を５枚用意してください。

ex.en: I need some cardboard boxes to pack my possessions.
ex.ja: 荷物をまとめるために、段ボールの箱が欲しいんです。

note.ja: card（厚紙）+ board（板）。「段ボール・厚紙」。

en: In a casual manner.

casually.ety: From Middle English casually, casuelly, casuali, casuely, equivalent to casual + -ly.

ex.en: You can talk to me casually.
ex.ja: タメ口でいいよ。

ex.en: Unless you prefer talking like this, you can speak to me casually.
ex.ja: この話し方が好きじゃなければ、カジュアルに話してくれていいよ。

ex.en: He picked up the newspaper and glanced casually over the front page.
ex.ja: 彼は新聞を取り上げて何気なく１面を眺めた。

note.ja: casual + -ly。「何気なく・くだけた服装で」。

en: To crush with the teeth by repeated closing and opening of the jaws; done to food to soften it and break it down by the action of saliva …
To grind, tear, or otherwise degrade or demolish something with teeth or as with teeth.
The act of chewing; mastication with the mouth.
Level of chewiness.

chew.ety: From Middle English chewen, from Old English ċēowan, from Proto-West Germanic *keuwan, from Proto-Germanic *kewwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁-. Cognate with West Frisian kôgje, Low German käwwen, Dutch kauwen, German kauen; also Latin gingīva (“gums”), Tocharian B śuwaṃ (“to eat”), Polish żuć (“to chew”), Persian جویدن (javidan), Pashto ژُوَل (žovạl, “to bite, gnaw”).

ex.en: You might as well chew your food well.
ex.ja: 食べ物はよくかむほうがよい。

ex.en: You may as well chew your food well.
ex.ja: 食べ物はよくかむほうがよい。

ex.en: I cannot chew. I do not have teeth.
ex.ja: 噛めないんだって。歯がないから。

note.ja: 古英語 cēowan（かむ）から。「かむ」。chewing gum。

en: Parallel, in the same vein, side by side.
Corresponding; accompanying, concomitant.
A security or guarantee (usually an asset) pledged for the repayment of a loan if one cannot procure enough funds to repay.
A branch of a bodily part or system of organs.

collateral.ety: Recorded since c.1378, from Old French, from Medieval Latin collaterālis, from Latin col- (“together with”) (a form of con-) + the stem of latus (“side”). By surface analysis, col- + lateral.

ex.en: We'll use the house as collateral so we can borrow some money.
ex.ja: 家を担保にお金を借りよう。

note.ja: ラテン語 col（共に）+ lateralis（側面の）。「横に並ぶ」→「付随的な」、借金の横に置く →「担保」。lateral と同じ。

en: An accumulation or buildup, the act of gathering into a heap or mass.
Blocking up of the capillary and other blood vessels, etc., in any locality or organ (often producing other morbid symptoms); local hyper…

congestion.ety: From late Middle English congestioun, from Old French [Term?], from Latin congestĭō (“heap, accumulation”), from congerō (“to bring together, accumulate, heap up”), formed by the root gerō (“to carry”) and the prefix con-.

ex.en: We know how to get around traffic congestion.
ex.ja: 私たちは交通渋滞をうまく避ける方法を知っている。

ex.en: Our delay was due to traffic congestion.
ex.ja: 私たちが遅れたのは交通が混雑していたからです。

ex.en: In spite of the terrible congestion, I was in time for the appointment.
ex.ja: ひどい渋滞にもかかわらず、私は定刻に間に合った。

note.ja: con（共に）+ gest（運ぶ）+ ion。一緒に運び込まれて詰まること →「混雑・渋滞・充血」。

en: A person to whom a debt is owed.
One who gives credence to something; a believer.

creditor.ety: From Middle English creditour, from Anglo-Norman creditour, from Latin crēditor, from crēditum (“loan”), from crēditus, perfect passive participle of crēdō (“lend”).

note.ja: credit（信用）+ -or。ラテン語 credere（信じる）。「信用して貸す人」→「債権者」。

en: A place where one thing crosses over another; a crossing.
The means by which a crossing is made.
Of an electrical cable, having connector pins at one end wired to different pins at the other; for example, pin 1 to pin 2, pin 2 to pin …
Configured so that the transmit signals at one end are connected to the receive signals at the other.

note.ja: cross over（横切る）の名詞化。「交差・ジャンルの融合」。

en: The time of daylight; the time between sunrise and sunset.
Pertaining to daytime; appropriate to the day.
Happening during the day.

en: The conveyance or transfer of an estate, either in fee for life or for years, most commonly the latter.
Transmission by formal act or conveyance to an heir or successor; transference; especially, the transfer or transmission of the crown or …
To convey, as by will or lease.
To transmit by inheritance.

demise.ety:
From Middle English demyse, dimise, dimisse, dymyse, from Middle French démise, the feminine singular past participle of démettre (“to put down, relinquish”); from Latin dēmissa, feminine singular of perfect passive participle of dēmittō. The "death" and "end" senses derive by way of euphemism from the legal sense, as a person's death was a common way that the legal demise could be accomplished.
The verb is from Middle English dimisen, from the noun.

note.ja: de（離れて）+ mis（送る）+ e。（地位・この世から）送り出されること →「死去・消滅」。

en: The state of being dependent, of relying upon another.
An irresistible physical or psychological need, especially for a chemical substance.

dependence.ety: From Middle French dépendance. Morphologically depend + -ence.

note.ja: de（下に）+ pend（ぶら下がる）+ ence。下にぶら下がること →「依存・頼ること」。

en: An authoritarian leader of a country, nation, or government.
A magistrate without colleague in republican Ancient Rome, who held full executive authority for a term granted by the Senate, typically …

ex.en: The whole nation cringed before this dictator in fear.
ex.ja: 全国民は恐怖からこの独裁者の前にひれ伏した。

ex.en: The people followed the dictator like so many sheep.
ex.ja: 民衆はまるで羊のように独裁者の後に従った。

en: Warning of bad consequences: ill-boding; portentous.
Requiring action to prevent bad consequences: urgent, pressing.

ex.en: You are a dire part of this.
ex.ja: 君は必要な人間なのだ。

ex.en: The economy is in dire need of a jump-start.
ex.ja: 経済は緊急に起爆剤を必要としています。

ex.en: I'm in dire need of money.
ex.ja: どうしてもお金が必要なんだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 dirus（恐ろしい）から。「悲惨な・差し迫った」。

en: An argument or debate.
A condition of not agreeing or concurring.

ex.en: Jim sometimes has disagreements with his wife.
ex.ja: ジムさんは時々、妻といさかいをする。

ex.en: The chairman did not rule out the possibility of a disagreement.
ex.ja: 議長は意見が不一致に終る可能性を排除しなかった。

ex.en: It sometimes is the case that there is a lot of disagreement.
ex.ja: 大きな意見の不一致があることが時々ある。

note.ja: dis（反対）+ agreement（一致）。「意見の相違」。
